body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1. Requested by the user off the review's "Minor" list.

## Problem

The server emits no security-relevant log events at all. There is no record of:

- failed and successful logins (and the device_label / platform claimed)
- logouts and session revocations
- password changes, email changes, account deletions
- admin actions: registration toggle, password reset of another account, user
  deletion — all of which are privileged and currently invisible after the fact
- invite mint / redeem / revoke
- authorization failures (403 not_a_member, 403 not_admin)

Consequences: a compromise leaves no trace to reconstruct; the operator cannot
tell a brute-force attempt from normal traffic; and the reverse-proxy
rate-limiting that server/README.md:334 makes mandatory has no application-level
signal to corroborate it. Nothing here is reconstructible from the database
after the fact, since the affected rows are mutated or deleted in place.

## Fix

Emit structured records through the stdlib logging module on a dedicated logger
(e.g. "shoppinglist_server.audit"), so a host app can route it to a file,
journald or syslog without the blueprint imposing a destination. A blueprint is
a guest in the host app — it should not configure handlers, only emit.

Each record should carry: timestamp, event type, account id (NOT email — see
below), source IP, and outcome.

Two things to get right:

- Do NOT log secrets or bearer tokens, not even truncated. Log the auth_tokens
  row id when a session must be identified.
- Do NOT log email addresses. The whole point of the account-id indirection is
  that logs then hold no PII, which matters given this is a personal-data store
  and logs are usually retained longer and guarded less than the database.
- Source IP is only trustworthy if the mandatory reverse proxy sets
  X-Forwarded-For AND the app is configured to honour it (werkzeug ProxyFix).
  Without that, every event logs the proxy's address. Either wire up ProxyFix in
  the host app and document it, or log no IP rather than a misleading one.

Document the logger name, the event vocabulary, and the retention/PII stance in
server/README.md, next to the existing "Deployment requirements" section.

## Verification

Tests asserting an event is emitted for each listed action, and — importantly —
a test asserting no bearer token and no email address ever appears in emitted
records.
title: audit trail: server emits no security-relevant log events
